conviction_note: Findings net to -0.4 (a company-level beat pattern and long-haul/fiber demand corroboration against counterparty capex trims at AT&T and Charter, MasTec's communications weakness and higher diesel); the evidence is balanced and mostly proxy, so p_up stays at 50 and the scaled move is 0, while abs_move_pct stays at the option-implied ~11.5 because the Q4 guide and FY27 update land with this print on a name whose last four reactions were -11.6, +25.8, -4.1, +9.8.
bar: Company Q3 FY27 guide (Aug 26, 2026): revenue $1.90-1.98B (mid $1.94B), adj. EBITDA $281-302M, adj. EPS $4.33-4.79 (mid $4.56) - https://dycomind.gcs-web.com/static-files/fa366b24-81e1-4e1e-8740-049667ed4577 and https://finviz.com/news/385718/dycom-industries-beats-q2-forecasts-as-digital-infrastructure-demand-accelerates . Street EPS is disputed: Earnings Whispers preview (2026-11-16) gives consensus $4.56 / revenue $1.92B and a whisper of $4.80 (https://finviz.com/news/423374/after-a-32-slide-dycom-must-prove-its-communications-margin-dip-was-temporary); another EW page $4.67; ChartMill $4.73 / $2.003B (likely stale, pre-guide). Sized against the company guide midpoint; print_vs_bar_pct is revenue vs $1.94B.
positioning_check: Short interest ~1.6M shares, 5.2% of shares outstanding, 2.5 days to cover as of 2026-11-16 (equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/dy/shortinterest); 4.8% of float / 3.0 days on 2026-08-19. Not a crowded short. Millennium Management filed a 13G for 5.4% (1,619,369 sh) with event date 2026-09-30 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/67215/000110465926114417/primary_doc.xml). 25d skew rejected by the baseline as implausible (-40.91 vol pts), so no usable directional statement from options; put/call OI 0.48 (call-heavy); event-implied move 11.26%, ATM IV 89%. Stock -53% over six months (StockStory 2026-11-05, $213.42, 13.1x forward P/E), -59% from 52w high, 13% above the 52w low; sentiment described as 'barely positive' (EW 2026-11-16). Sector peer MasTec fell 59.5% May 8-Nov 4 2026.

findings.finding: Dycom has beaten its own EPS guide at or above the top end two quarters running: Q1 FY27 release headline 'Exceeds High End of Fiscal Q1 2027 Outlook', and Q2 FY27 adj. EPS $5.29 against a May guide of $4.40-4.82 (top end +9.8%) and consensus $4.70, with Q2 revenue $2.006B against a $1.94-2.01B guide (which excluded NTI's $22.9M). The Q3 guide is $4.33-4.79 EPS / $1.90-1.98B revenue, consensus sits at the $4.56 midpoint (EW), so the same pattern would put Q3 adj. EPS near or above $4.79 and revenue near $1.97B, roughly +5% EPS / +1.5% revenue vs the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY27 (2026-08-26) beat EPS by ~12% vs consensus and above the guide top, and the stock fell -11.6% on the day (and ~-32% over the following streak) because the Q3 guide midpoint sat below consensus and comms margin fell; Q1 FY27 (2026-05-27) beat-and-raise bought +25.8%. The beat alone has not been paid; the guide decides.
findings.why_not_priced: The whisper ($4.80, EW 2026-11-16) already sits at the guide top, so part of the beat pattern is priced; consensus at $4.56 has drifted down from $4.67 to the guide midpoint. If the market fully priced a repeat of the Q2 overshoot (~+10% vs guide top) the whisper would be above $5.00.
findings.independence: Q2 guide figures from https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2943843/dycom-industries-dy-down-7-8-since-last-earnings-report-can-it-rebound and Q1 release https://dycomind.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dycom-industries-inc-reports-record-first-quarter-results-and ; same company, so this is one company-level pattern, not two signals.

findings.finding: US on-highway diesel (EIA) rose from $5.35-5.45/gal in August 2026 (week of Aug 17: $5.454, the level when the Q3 guide was set on Aug 26) to $6.28 (Oct 20) and $6.35 (Oct 26), roughly +15-17% across Dycom's Aug-Oct quarter; management attributed ~35 bp of the Q2 Communications margin decline (13.6% vs 14.9%) to fuel, so Q3 comms margin carries an extra fuel headwind beyond the guide-date spot price, on the exact line the stock sold off on in August.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Communications adj. EBITDA margin (13.6%, -134 bp y/y, ~35 bp of it fuel) was the line cited for the -11.6% reaction on 2026-08-26 (Nasdaq/Motley Fool, EW preview).
findings.why_not_priced: Previews (EW 2026-11-16) cite the Q2 fuel hit but no one quantifies Q3 fuel; if priced, the EPS consensus would sit below the guide midpoint rather than at it. Scale is small: a further ~20-30 bp on ~$1.6B of comms revenue is ~$3-5M of EBITDA against a $21M-wide guide range, so it most likely lands inside the guide.
findings.independence: August EIA levels from https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/?g=1XTvU and Logistics Management weekly reports; fuel attribution from the Q2 call (https://finviz.com/news/423374/after-a-32-slide-dycom-must-prove-its-communications-margin-dip-was-temporary). Proxy: macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by Dycom for Q3.

findings.finding: MasTec (reported 2026-10-29, after Dycom last spoke) said communications customers delayed capital-spending decisions on uncertainty over a potential fourth nationwide wireless carrier and reorganizations at major customers; its Communications revenue fell 11.8% y/y to $806.9M, EBITDA -40.7%, margin -370 bp, and it framed 2027 communications revenue as roughly flat. Dycom already deferred ~$150M of wireless revenue from 2H FY27 into FY28, so the read-through is risk of further wireless slippage in the Q4 guide / FY27 update.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The wireless deferral and comms margin drove the -11.6% August reaction and the subsequent 32% slide; Q3 FY26 (2025-11-19) raised FY outlook and bought +9.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: DY fell to a 52-week low around this period (Oct 20, Nov 5). If fully priced the Q3 EPS consensus would have dropped below the guide midpoint; it sits at it. Net of the rest of the company: Dycom's communications grew 16.7% organically in Q2 with FTTH up ~60% in 1H and $12.2B backlog, while MasTec cited its own wireline execution problems, so much of MTZ's weakness is MTZ-specific; sized small for that.
findings.independence: Segment numbers: https://zacks.com/stock/news/3019447/mastec-q3-earnings-revenues-beat-estimates-on-power-delivery-strength ; fourth-carrier context (SpaceX talks for ~80,000 sites, Bloomberg via 24/7 Wall St, 2026-10-23): https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/23/spacex-is-coming-for-the-phone-companies-but-the-tower-owners-win-either-way . Peer, not a counterparty.

findings.finding: AT&T, Dycom's largest customer, on 2026-10-21 lowered its long-term capital investment outlook to $22-23B a year for 2027 and 2028 (about $1B below the prior plan, roughly two-thirds attributed to fiber build 'efficiencies' and one-third to the Mexico sale), while keeping 2026 at $23-24B and the 60M+ fiber locations by 2030 target, and announced a GIP/CPP joint venture to build fiber outside its footprint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Dycom reaction to an AT&T capex cut in the baseline; Dycom's FY commentary on FTTH demand has been the swing line in raise quarters (+25.8% May 2026, +9.8% Nov 2025).
findings.why_not_priced: It is public for a month and DY has drifted with it; what is not visible is how Dycom will frame FY28 AT&T volumes or pricing under 'construction efficiencies' when asked on the call. If priced as a volume cut, FY28 estimates would have come down; previews still frame FY28 as a wireless-recovery year. The 2026 spend (DY's current quarter and Q4) is unchanged, and the fiber locations target is unchanged, so the size is small.
findings.independence: Morningstar note on the ~$1B cut and its split: https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/att-earnings-trimming-fair-value-estimate-higher-assumed-spectrum-costs ; release summary https://finviz.com/news/405039/att-delivers-strong-third-quarter-2026-results-with-its-best-consolidated-service-revenue-growth-in-more-than-four-years (same company, one finding).

findings.finding: Charter (2026-11-06) cut pro forma line-extension capex to $807M in Q3 2026 from $1,254M a year earlier and subsidized rural line-extension capex to $292M from $580M, while upgrade/rebuild rose to $757M from $520M; it launched a 'new operating model' with $2B of run-rate opex cuts over 18 months, guides 2026 pro forma capex ~$13.0B, and per a call summary sees 2027 at or below $11B.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline reaction tied to a cable-customer capex change; Charter is one of the major customers MasTec described as reorganizing.
findings.why_not_priced: Arrived after Dycom's last update and after the 2026-10-29 peer read. The rural (RDOF) wind-down was scheduled and is known, and the upgrade/rebuild increase is work Dycom also performs, so the net for Dycom is mixed; if fully negative for DY the stock would not have bounced from $192.79 (Nov 5) to $218 since.
findings.independence: 2027 capex '<= $11B' only from a transcript summary (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262292936-), not in the release; TelecomLead summary https://telecomlead.com/broadband/charter-q3-2026-capex-falls-11-2-to-3-2-billion-broadband-subscribers-drop-to-34-3-million-spectrum-mobile-reaches-13-5-million-128591?amp=1 (same document).

findings.finding: Counterparty evidence since Dycom last spoke corroborates the fiber and long-haul demand its $12.2B backlog rests on: Verizon (2026-10-26) held 2026 capex at $16.0-16.5B with fiber net adds of 155k vs 61k a year earlier; Lumen (Q3 2026) hit its 5M new PCF-funded fiber-mile target more than two months early and signed additional PCF deals; MasTec booked ~2,100 miles of hyperscaler-linked long-haul fiber in and after Q3, construction from mid-2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog/long-haul commentary was the positive line in the May 2026 +25.8% reaction; in August a record backlog did not offset the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The sector de-rated through this news (MTZ -59.5% May-Nov; DY -53% in six months), so demand corroboration has not been rewarded in the price; if it were, DY would not be at 13.1x forward earnings with a record backlog. Mostly timing for FY28 rather than the quarter, hence small.
findings.independence: Lumen: https://finviz.com/news/415789/lumen-technologies-reports-solid-third-quarter-2026-results-strategic-growth-and-operating-leverage-gain-momentum ; MasTec fiber miles: https://finviz.com/news/412769/mastecs-record-backlog-outruns-pipeline-and-communications-stumbles-but-a-36-slide-shows-investors-want-proof (MasTec is also the source of the negative comms finding; the two readings are of different lines: wireless/carrier delays vs hyperscaler long-haul).

findings.finding: Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, FL on 2026-10-08 as a Category 2 and knocked out power to 610,000+ customers in Florida and Alabama, with restoration through ~Oct 16, inside Dycom's fiscal Q3 (ends ~Oct 31); storm restoration work is incremental revenue not in the Aug 26 guide.
findings.why_not_priced: No preview mentions storm work; it is small relative to $1.9B revenue and Dycom's telecom restoration share is unknown, so at most a few tens of millions of revenue at low margin.
findings.independence: S&P Global on restoration crews: https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/electric-power/101326-thousands-work-in-south-to-restore-power-to-customers-in-isaias-wake ; proxy, unconfirmed by Dycom.

findings.finding: After the Democratic midterm sweep (Nov 4-5, 2026), AI data-center and infrastructure stocks sold off on fears of tighter permitting; UBS estimated ~30% of expected 2028 US data-center capacity additions at risk from construction pauses. Dycom itself flagged local data-center moratoriums and community opposition as a risk on its Q2 call, and its Building Systems (inside-the-fence) and long-haul to data centers lines are exposed; the call will be the first time management addresses it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Building Systems margin (24.5%) and data-center backlog were positives in Q2; no reaction history on a permitting statement.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: DY's 52-week low ($192.79) was set Nov 5 and MasTec fell 15.4% on Nov 4. What is unpriced is Dycom's own answer; a reassuring backlog statement would relieve, a cautious one would confirm. Two-sided, small.
findings.independence: Trefis on MTZ -15.4% Nov 4 on AI data-center sentiment: https://www.trefis.com/articles/622874/does-the-fall-in-mastec-stock-change-anything/2026-11-05 ; Dycom moratorium risk from EW preview https://finviz.com/news/423374/after-a-32-slide-dycom-must-prove-its-communications-margin-dip-was-temporary .

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is washed out rather than crowded: shares down 53.3% over six months to $213 (13.1x forward P/E) on 2026-11-05, sentiment 'barely positive', EPS consensus already cut from $4.67 to the $4.56 guide midpoint, short interest only 5.2% / 2.5 days, and a new $150M buyback authorized in August.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 (Nov 2025) after a drawdown: +9.8%; August 2026 into a crowded-bullish setup: -11.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a statement about the price itself, so by construction it is the bar rather than information; it is filed small because the bar the stock must clear is lower than in August, not because the stock is cheap.

findings.finding: Insiders bought after the August drop and have not sold into it: CEO Dan Peyovich bought 850 shares (~$252k, ~$297/sh) and director David Fallon 700 shares at $286.92 on 2026-09-01; the only post-drop sale notice is director Jennifer Fritzsche's Form 144 for 1,000 RSU-derived shares (~$212k) on 2026-11-05; Nov 2-3 director Form 4s are 'A'-coded grants (e.g., 197 shares at $221.05).
findings.why_not_priced: Purchases were made ~$70 above today's price, so they say little about the Q3 print specifically; small token sizes.

outside_window.finding: SpaceX's spectrum purchase / fourth-carrier plan (talks for ~80,000 US cell sites) is expected to close in 1H 2027 pending approval; resolution of the 'fourth carrier' uncertainty MasTec cited as delaying carrier capex lands after this window.

MasTec's ~2,100 miles of hyperscaler long-haul fiber begin construction around mid-2027, and AT&T's GIP/CPP out-of-territory fiber JV builds later; these are FY28 volume drivers for the industry, not visible in this print except as commentary.

rejected_candidates.detail: Folded into the demand-corroboration finding (Verizon/Lumen/MasTec long-haul); the sources found are July/August-dated, before Dycom last spoke.

Recorded in positioning_check; a multi-strategy holder's passive filing carries no direction on its own.

baseline_tension: No usable skew (rejected), call-heavy open interest and a stock already 53% down with the sector argue the bar is low, while the counterparty evidence since August (MasTec comms, AT&T 2027-28 capex, Charter line extensions, diesel) leans mildly against the guide; the two roughly offset, so nothing here contradicts an 11% two-sided implied move.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a reaction): beat-pattern finding cut +1.0 -> +0.6 because the Q2 beat above the guide top was sold -11.6% on the guide.
Lesson 6 (inside the guide): diesel finding cut -0.7 -> -0.4; the likely EBITDA effect (~$3-5M) lands inside a $21M-wide guide range.
Lesson 9 (net of the rest): MasTec comms read-through cut -1.0 -> -0.7; Dycom's communications grew 16.7% organically with FTTH +~60% while MTZ cited its own execution problems.
Lesson 5 (proxy vs counterparty document): AT&T capex finding kept as a direct-counterparty document but cut -0.8 -> -0.6 because the 2026 spend that drives this quarter and Q4 is unchanged.
Lesson 5 / definition ('cheap is not a finding'): positioning finding cut +0.5 -> +0.3 and reworded as a lower bar, not an undervaluation call.
Left standing: Charter -0.4, demand corroboration +0.7, hurricane +0.2, midterm permitting -0.3, insiders +0.2; abs_move_pct 11.5 and p_up 50 unchanged.
